result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as a mock-resources folder, whatever the rest of its name is. I haven't run the three new cases (plain `mock/`, `mock.data`, `mock-größe`) or the must-not-match cases, because I didn't add tests. The existing scoping and convention tests in `codeanalyzer` pass.

In `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`, I changed the regexes on lines 393–394:
- `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` is now `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*`.
- `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` is now `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`.

- **Why this fixes the three cases:** The old character class needed at least one ASCII letter, digit, underscore, hyphen or space after `mock`, so it missed plain `mock/`, `mock.data` and `mock(old)`, and non-ASCII names such as `mock模拟`. `[^/]*` accepts anything, including nothing.
- **Windows paths:** `SourceFileFilter.matches` already normalises backslashes to forward slashes before matching, so those paths work without further changes.
- **What stays out:** `remock/`, `demo/` and `src/main/java/` don't match, because the pattern needs a `/` immediately before `mock`. `mock.java` and `mockery.java` are files, not folders, so the trailing `/` rules them out.
- **What stays in:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` all still match.
